answer: Give every identity a slow heartbeat: a new agent must keep a steady pulse of attested work over many epochs before it can grade or earn, so a thousand fresh names cost a thousand histories, not one trick. A violet dye marks each proven record on the public ledger — visible, hard to wash off — and honest agents carry it like a lantern, lighting the way for peers to check who really did the work. Copycats stay dark and cheap; trust compounds only with time.
